segments: 446 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
the capital of that province was Gurganj.
And when some of the Tatars,
those who were accustomed to go in advance of the armies,
reached the gate of the city,
the citizens thought that these few were all alone,
and a great multitude of people, horsemen and foot soldiers, went out from the city to encounter those Tatars.
And when they reached a certain vineyard called Kowram,
which was one stadium distant,
the army of the Mongols fell upon them,
and killed them all.
Those citizens who were destroyed and fell upon the earth numbered about one hundred thousand.
And the Tatars came masterfully,
and easily took control of the city,
and laid it waste,
and also destroyed the rest of its population.
Sultan Muhammad, however, had already left and crossed over to the land of Khorasan,
and constantly took counsel with his grandees,
saying, "What expedient do we have,
and how shall we be delivered from the hands of this powerful enemy?" And they were saying
that hope had been cut off for him from the regions beyond the Gihon (Oxus),
"It is only here in Khorasan that places of refuge must be prepared,
and armies be made ready for their battle if they come."
And he was saying:
"We have no heart left for battle with these people,
and if they cross over against us, we have no choice
except to flee before them to India."
His son, however, Jalal al-Din Khwarizmshah, did not consent to flee,
but rather that they should all fight until they died in battle.
His father, however, rebuked him for this,
and as one who was soon destined to die,
he began to eat {OCR? g-m'kal -> l-m'kal} and to drink and to delight in worldly pleasures,
as if to have his fill of them.
And while he was occupied with this,
he heard that the Tatars had crossed the waters of the Gihon.
And he abandoned [everything] and fled toward Hamadan,
and he sent his wives and his small children to the fortress called Balan {Ilal?}.
And when the Tatars reached Hamadan,
the Sultan fled into the mountains toward Mazandaran.
And when they overtook him there as well,
he fled and entered one of the islands of the Hyrcanian Sea (Caspian Sea),
and there he remained until news came to him
that the Tatars had taken control of that fortress in which his family was,
and that they had taken captive his wives, his sons, and his daughters;
